To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pupils from upper class families are more likely to study abroad than those from working class families.
pupils from upper-class families with high levels of embodied and cultural transnational capital have a higher chance of planning to study abroad.

(a) the plans to study abroad of pupils from upper-class backgrounds are due to their transnational activities, (b) the plans to go abroad of pupils attending internationalised streams and gymnasiums are due to their socialisation into transnational cultural capital, (c) the plans to leave the country of pupils attending international streams are not due to the school's international character, and (d) there is a strong social reproduction of transnational capital.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social reproduction of transnational capital and its relation to the reproduction of class.
the social reproduction of transnational cultural capital, which is embodied in the plans to study abroad of Dutch pupils.
the social reproduction of transnational capital, which is a relatively new form of cultural capital.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social reproduction of transnational capital is not as strong as the reproduction of other capitals.
the social reproduction of transnational capital in Dutch education is limited, but that it does exist.
the decision to pursue a study abroad is part and parcel of the social reproduction of transnational capital.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plans to study abroad are related to social class position and the transnational activities of pupils and their parents.
the plans to study abroad were related to social reproduction.
pupils’ plans to study abroad are related to their family’s transnational capital and to the school type they attended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social class and transnational activities are important factors in the decision to study in another country.
social reproduction is not limited to national contexts, but is also a transnational phenomenon.
the social reproduction of transnational capital is an important factor in the social reproduction of higher education.
